reconcile.note: Gill reads Joel's rebuke as relative rather than absolute, ranking heart-rending above garment-rending rather than forbidding the outward sign outright.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses the tension directly, since scripture both praises Josiah for tearing his clothes and has Joel forbid the practice and Elisha rebuke a king for it.

sides.snippet: have torn your clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard you, says Yahweh.
sides.verseText: because your heart was tender, and you did humble yourself before Yahweh, when you heard what I spoke against this place, and against the inhabitants of it, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and have torn your clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard you, says Yahweh.

sides.snippet: Tear your heart, and not your garments
sides.verseText: Tear your heart, and not your garments, And turn to Yahweh, your God; For he is gracious and merciful, Slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, And relents from sending calamity.
